boundary.independent_change: Evidence can be refined before accepted product requirements change.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted problem evidence and unresolved discovery questions.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Evidence and observations about the problem space.

authorities.responsibility: Own problem observations, actors, desired outcomes and motivating evidence without deciding product requirements or solution semantics.

boundary.independent_change: Product intent can change without directly deciding domain or technical realization.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted behavioral and acceptance semantics to downstream design.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Decisions about what the product must achieve.

authorities.responsibility: Own accepted product intent, scope, externally observable behavior, constraints and acceptance expectations.

boundary.independent_change: Strategic classification can change without redefining model-context relationships or tactical realization.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted subdomain landscape and strategic classification to relevant downstream consumers.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Strategic decisions about domain responsibilities and investment.

authorities.responsibility: Own problem-space domain decomposition, subdomain landscape, strategic classification and domain investment intent without deciding model-language boundaries or tactical structures.

boundary.independent_change: Context boundaries and translations can change while strategic domain classification remains stable.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted model-context and translation knowledge to tactical, application and interface consumers.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Model-language applicability, context relationships and translation contracts.

authorities.responsibility: Own where models/languages apply and how independently modeled contexts relate or translate without re-owning domain investment strategy or tactical internals.

boundary.independent_change: Tactical semantics can evolve behind stable strategic/use-case contracts without selecting storage or transport.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted tactical domain semantics to application and technical design.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Decisions about how accepted domain behavior is modeled semantically.

authorities.responsibility: Own tactical domain language, identities, lifecycles, invariants, decisions and public domain semantics.

boundary.independent_change: Application composition can evolve without re-owning underlying domain truth or technical architecture.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted application flows and orchestration semantics.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Decisions about orchestration across domain responsibilities and user/system journeys.

authorities.responsibility: Own application-level composition of accepted domain/product behavior.

boundary.independent_change: Architecture can evolve behind stable product/domain contracts without changing their semantic ownership.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted system topology and architectural constraints.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Structural and runtime decisions that constrain implementation.

authorities.responsibility: Own system structure, runtime boundaries, dependency topology and technical interaction topology.

boundary.independent_change: Concurrency semantics can change when execution/delivery behavior changes while system decomposition remains stable.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted concurrency/consistency constraints to data, component, implementation and verification consumers.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Ordering, isolation, atomicity, conflict, retry/idempotency and consistency semantics for interacting executions.

authorities.responsibility: Own concurrent-state correctness contracts without re-owning domain invariants, storage representation or system topology.

boundary.independent_change: Security architecture can evolve independently from product/domain entitlement semantics, interface representation and later threat analysis.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted security constraints to system/interface/data/component/operability/verification/implementation consumers without re-owning their semantics.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Decisions about security trust boundaries, trusted identity, credential/session protection, admission and enforcement structure.

authorities.responsibility: Own security-specific trust, identity, admission, protection and enforcement structure derived from accepted product, domain and system truth.

boundary.independent_change: Machine interface contracts can evolve while preserving accepted product/domain semantics and human interaction design.
boundary.public_contract: Provides canonical machine interface contracts to integrations and technical consumers.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Machine-consumed protocol, API, message and representation semantics.

authorities.responsibility: Own supported external machine interaction and representation contracts.

boundary.independent_change: Human interface realization can evolve while product/domain and machine-interface semantics remain stable.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted human-interface and presentation/view contracts to architecture, component, implementation and test consumers.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Human interaction, information/navigation structure, presentation system and screen/view composition.

authorities.responsibility: Own human interaction semantics and presentation/view composition without re-owning product behavior or machine interface contracts.

boundary.independent_change: Storage design can evolve behind stable domain/application contracts.
boundary.public_contract: Provides accepted persistence model and storage constraints.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Decisions about durable physical data representation and constraints.

authorities.responsibility: Own physical persistence and storage representation.

boundary.independent_change: Quality constraints can evolve without reallocating semantic ownership.
boundary.public_contract: Provides measurable or explicitly unresolved quality constraints to architecture, implementation and verification.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Cross-cutting non-functional constraints on realization.

authorities.responsibility: Own explicit realization quality constraints derived from accepted product/design truth.

boundary.independent_change: Threat knowledge and coverage can evolve without itself owning product/domain/security/system/interface/data decisions.
boundary.public_contract: Provides security coverage evidence, verification obligations and blocking Questions; it never silently repairs missing upstream design.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Analysis of applicable threats, accepted controls, not-applicable/deferred concerns and unresolved security gaps against an accepted design baseline.

authorities.responsibility: Own threat, control and applicability coverage against accepted design and route material gaps to the Authority that owns their resolution.

boundary.independent_change: Operability evidence can evolve without redefining product/domain/interface semantics or selecting telemetry implementation mechanics.
boundary.public_contract: Provides runtime evidence requirements to component, verification/test and implementation consumers while routing configuration, failure, security and reliability semantics to their owning Authorities.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Decisions about what runtime evidence must exist so accepted behavior, lifecycle state and technical failure are diagnosable.

authorities.responsibility: Own runtime evidence and diagnosability requirements derived from accepted product, architecture, interface, security and quality truth.

boundary.independent_change: Engineering discipline can be refined without redefining product/domain semantics, while downstream realization may require reevaluation.
boundary.public_contract: Provides reviewable engineering obligations to applicable design and implementation consumers.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Normative cross-cutting rules for how accepted engineering knowledge may be realized.

authorities.responsibility: Own project-selected engineering design obligations and explicit anti-pattern constraints without owning the project semantics to which they apply.

boundary.independent_change: Component realization can evolve behind accepted architecture/application/interface contracts without changing their semantics.
boundary.public_contract: Provides code-design boundaries sufficient for implementation agents to avoid inventing architecturally significant structure.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Public component responsibilities, consumer/provider contracts, dependency direction, abstraction ownership and composition/mapping boundaries.

authorities.responsibility: Own implementation-facing component decomposition and dependency contracts without deciding implementation sequencing or private code structure.

boundary.independent_change: Test contracts can survive changes in implementation slicing, code structure, frameworks and test mechanics while accepted behavior remains stable.
boundary.public_contract: Provides traceable executable test semantics sufficient for test-first or implementation work without allowing tests to invent upstream truth.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Preconditions, controlled operations, observable oracles, invariants, state transitions, failure/atomicity distinctions and property/state-machine obligations.

authorities.responsibility: Own executable observable test contracts derived from accepted verification and semantic design without owning production semantics or concrete test-code mechanics.

boundary.independent_change: Realization order, physical mapping and replaceable tools can change without redefining upstream truth when accepted boundaries and obligations remain satisfied.
boundary.public_contract: Provides implementation plan, repository/tooling realization, quality-gate wiring and completion criteria while routing missing semantic decisions upstream.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Decisions about how accepted design will be realized as bounded implementation work and a reproducible physical codebase/toolchain.

authorities.responsibility: Own implementation slicing, sequencing, repository realization, concrete toolchain/gate wiring and completion criteria after upstream engineering decisions are available.

boundary.independent_change: Verification strategy can evolve without taking ownership of product/domain/architecture semantics.
boundary.public_contract: Provides verification strategy and acceptance evidence; routes design gaps to owning Authorities.
boundary.semantic_cohesion: Decisions about what executable or inspectable evidence proves accepted design.

authorities.responsibility: Own verification levels, traceability, scenarios and evidence proving implementation realizes accepted engineering knowledge.

consumers.purpose: Determine the engineering knowledge required to realize the accepted PREP frontend implementation target from frozen Reference Engineering Model v0 and accepted project truth.
